contract: Socket.IO outgoing stream_ready: normally no event; when a reset's retranscode finishes before its delayed segment check starts, the check emits stream_ready once with a single null argument to every socket of the owning user and to no other socket.
exceptions: force is not applicable: the event has no force/refresh trigger; it can only come from a segment check after a reset.

Normal completion clears the segment check and therefore emits no stream_ready; the positive path needs a reset whose retranscode finishes before the delayed check starts. Both silence scenarios listen for 3 s on every audience socket — past the 2 s segment-check interval (server/objects/Stream.js:222-230) — so a still-running loop cannot pass by chance.
The accepted playback lifecycle packet supplies scoped evidence and documents that stream_ready is not part of normal completion; its Go differences are deliberately not asserted here.

invariants.contract: A normal completed transcode emits stream_open but no stream_ready on any socket, and a stream that fails on its input emits stream_error with no stream_ready.

After a missing segment before the start offset resets a stream whose retranscode finishes before the delayed check, stream_ready is emitted once with a single null argument on both sockets of the owner and on no admin or other-user socket; a second reset of a second session emits its own single stream_ready.
